good: Round, biodegradable wax beads that roll dead skin off without scratching.
care: Low risk.

name: Chia seeds
good: Soaked or blended, they release a slippery gel that adds slip and soft hold.
care: Strain well so seeds don't stick in hair.

name: Desiccated coconut (ground)
good: Dried coconut; a soft, fragrant scrub grain.
care: Can clog drains; use a little.

name: Menthol crystals
good: Gives balms a strong cooling feel, as in chest rubs.
care: Keep it to 5% or less, away from eyes and inside the nose. Not for children under 6, where it can affect breathing.

name: Camphor
good: Warming, cooling scent in chest and muscle rubs.
care: Toxic if swallowed, even in small amounts. Keep it to about 3% or less, store out of children's reach, and never use it on children under 6, broken skin, or in pregnancy.

name: Xanthan gum
good: Thickens water-based gels and washes at 0.3 to 1%.
care: It thickens but doesn't preserve. Anything with water still needs a preservative.

name: Marshmallow root
good: Gives a slippery, detangling feel when simmered in water.
care: Low risk. The tea spoils like any tea.

name: Citric acid powder
good: A clean, consistent acid for sugaring paste in place of lemon juice.
care: For cooked sugar wax only. Don't put the powder or a homemade solution on skin; its strength is hard to control.

name: Lemon juice
care: Very acidic, and in sunlight it causes blistering burns and dark patches that can last for months. The one exception is cooked sugaring paste, where it's cooked into the sugar and removed with the hair.

name: Lime juice
care: Causes phytophotodermatitis: sun-triggered burns and long-lasting dark streaks. Only acceptable cooked into sugaring paste.

name: Baking soda
care: Strongly alkaline. It strips the skin's protective acid layer and causes dryness and irritation.

name: Apple cider vinegar
care: Undiluted vinegar has caused chemical burns. At most, use it heavily diluted in a rinse-off product.

name: Raw garlic
care: Causes chemical burns on skin, even with short contact.

name: Toothpaste
care: Irritates skin and can cause a rash. It's not made for use on skin.

name: Hydrogen peroxide
care: Damages healthy skin cells and slows wound healing.

name: Black henna
care: Usually contains PPD, a hair dye chemical that can cause blistering burns, scarring, and a lifelong allergy to hair dye. Real henna is never black.

name: Traditional kohl (khol, kajal, surma, tiro)
care: Many traditional kohls are made from galena, which is lead sulfide. Lab tests often find high lead levels, and lead poisoning in children has been traced to kohl. Use a cosmetic eyeliner sold under your country's cosmetics rules instead.

name: Lye (sodium hydroxide)
care: Needed to make real bar soap, but on its own it causes severe chemical burns and can blind. Wear goggles and gloves, always add lye to water, and run every recipe through a lye calculator. In finished, cured soap, none of it remains.

name: Lamp soot (homemade kajal)
care: Soot from a lamp or candle isn't purified carbon. It can carry tar and other combustion residues, and homemade kajal isn't sterile, so it can cause eye infections. Use a commercial kajal sold under cosmetics rules.

name: Rubbing alcohol
care: Strips oil so hard that skin often overcorrects with more oil, and it leaves skin dry and irritated. Not a mask ingredient.

name: School glue (peel-off masks)
care: Peel-off glue masks rip away skin cells and fine hairs, and can leave skin raw and inflamed. They don't pull out blackheads.

name: Store bar soap (grated)
good: Finished bar soap can be grated and melted with a little water into a new bar (rebatching). It's already made, so there's no lye to handle.
care: Check the label first: skip "beauty soaps" that list mercury (mercurous chloride, calomel) or have no ingredient list. Actives like kojic acid mostly rinse off.

name: Store-bought lotion or cream
good: A finished, preserved cream you can mix a little oil or butter into for a richer feel.
care: Its preservative was tested at full strength. Don't add water, juice or fresh ingredients, and mix small batches. Never blend in steroid, hydroquinone or unlabelled lightening creams.

name: Gum arabic (acacia gum)
good: A natural gum that dissolves in water and dries to a light, smooth film; it also thickens masks and gels.
care: It thickens but doesn't preserve. Mix fresh. Rarely, people react to acacia.

name: Corn starch
good: Thickens soap pastes and scrub balls and absorbs sweat in body powders.
care: It's food for microbes once wet, so anything with starch and water spoils faster. Skip on skin prone to yeast rashes.

name: "White henna" (الحناء البيضاء)
flag: "White henna" isn't henna: check the label
care: Real henna only stains orange-red, so "white henna" is a blend whose contents vary by seller. Use only one with a full ingredient list, and patch test for 2 days.

name: Strawberry seeds
good: Tiny, round seeds that give a gentle, even polish in body and lip scrubs.
care: Use a teaspoon or so per batch; lots of seeds can collect in drains.

name: Fine cornmeal
good: A medium, rounded grit for body and foot scrubs. Cheap and doesn't dissolve.
care: Body and feet only. Keep it dry; wet cornmeal spoils.

name: Pink (Himalayan) salt, fine
good: Same job as sea salt; the pink colour is from trace iron. Pick fine grain for scrubs.
care: Stings cuts and freshly shaved skin. Body only. The mineral and detox claims aren't backed by research.

name: Bamboo stem powder
good: A fine, soft, plant-based exfoliant that doesn't dissolve; gentle enough for face scrubs.
care: Rub lightly, once or twice a week on the face.

name: Walnut shell powder

care: Crushed shell has jagged edges that can cause tiny tears, so keep it off the face and go gently. It's a tree nut: skip with a nut allergy.

name: Pumice powder
